newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends down on RBI action, but off lows.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends down on RBI action, but off lows.

text.p: The Indian rupee recovered in afternoon trade to end Wednesday at 35.865/875 per dollar, weakening from Tuesday's close at 35.830/835 as central bank dollar purchases continued, dealers said.
The rupee traded at an early high of 35.84 and a low of 35.89 on Wednesday, with some stray deals at 35.895, dealers said.
They said Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases pushed the rupee down but with dollar supply good the Indian currency was safe from any threat of a sudden plunge.
"What is happening at the moment is that once the RBI goes off the market, the rupee bounces back," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Dollar supply continues to exceed demand."
RBI dollar purchases have pushed the rupee down to its current level from the weekend close of 35.745/755.
Dealers said the RBI bought dollars on a number of occasions on Wednesday but the quantum seemed to be less than Tuesday's.
While detailed figures are not available, dealers estimate the RBI bought a total of around $300-400 million on Monday and Tuesday.
"Today they would have bought $100 million, $150 at the most," said a dealer.
Dealers said the RBI bought dollars upto 35.88 rupees on Wednesday.
The rupee strengthened against the forward dollar on dollar sales as domestic liquidity eased and corporates booked profits at higher levels by selling dollars.
Call money eased on Wednesday to close at 7.5-8.5 percent, down from a high of 10.5 on Monday on imrpoved liquidity following the RBI's dollar purchases.
"Call is down, sentiment is soft on forwards, said a dealer. "Further we saw some selling of forward dollars by corporates as they looked to book profits.
November delivery dollars ended Wednesday at a premium of 93/96 paise against Tuesday's close of 98/100, dealers said.
The Indian forex market is largely inactive on Thursday as banks in the commercial capital of Bombay are closed for a local holiday. Banks reopen on Friday.
